title: Effects of a Virtual Reality Headset During Ultrasound-Guided Vacuum-Assisted Breast Biopsy on Pain - A Randomized Controlled Trial
summary:
Medications for pain and anxiety during medical procedures can cause side effects and are often complex to administer. A promising alternative is the use of a Virtual Reality (VR) headset, which directs the patient's attention toward a relaxing scenario, thereby reducing the perception of pain. Ultrasound-guided vacuum-assisted breast biopsy is a minimally invasive outpatient procedure lasting approximately 5–20 minutes, performed under local anaesthesia. The patient lies on a treatment table while the biopsy needle is guided to the target lesion under ultrasound control. A VR headset displaying calming scenarios, such as a walk on the beach or a journey through space, can be used in this setting to provide targeted distraction and relaxation.
This randomised controlled trial investigates whether the use of the CE-marked VR headset HypnoVR® during the procedure reduces pain, anxiety, and stress, and improves patient satisfaction. In addition, medical staff will be surveyed regarding their satisfaction with the use of the VR headset.
conditions: Evaluation or excision of breast lesions with benign or uncertain malignant potential

interventions.name: Intervention group: Patients undergoing ultrasound-guided vacuum-assisted breast biopsy while wearing the CE-marked VR headset HypnoVR®.
Control group: Patients undergoing the same procedure without the use of a VR headset.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Sufficient knowledge of German (spoken and written) for independent communication and for understanding the study information and informed consent form
Written informed consent after explanation
Planned outpatient ultrasound-guided vacuum-assisted breast biopsy under local anaesthesia
Sonographically clearly localizable lesion
No contraindication to local anaesthetic
Exclusion criteria:
Insufficient knowledge of German (spoken and written) preventing understanding of the study information or provision of informed consent
Expected lack of patient compliance or inability of the patient to understand the purpose and objectives of the clinical trial
Missing patient consent
Needle or claustrophobia
Advanced dementia or cognitive impairment (clinical assessment: inability to provide informed consent or to follow instructions)
Pregnancy
Clinically relevant coagulation disorder (INR >1.5; platelet count <100,000/µL)
Acute infection in the biopsy area with erythema
Neurological pre-existing conditions (migraine, epilepsy, known motion sickness)
Eye conditions significantly impairing the use of the VR headset (e.g., advanced macular degeneration, severe cataract)
Positional vertigo
